problem: Prior LLM-based generalist agents (PaLM-E, RT-2, LLaVA-style VLMs) mostly take 2D images and rarely handle tasks defined in 3D, such as grounding, embodied reasoning and acting. Prior 3D VL models (3D-VisTA, 3D-LLM) rely on task-specific heads or fine-tuning, cannot act, and suffer from scarce, hallucination-prone 3D-language data.
motivation: Generalist models have succeeded in 2D through large data plus scalable Transformers, but real-world tasks need an agent that understands and interacts with 3D scenes. Scaling 3D-language data is hard because manual 3D annotation is expensive. LLM-generated 3D data from bounding-box prompts (3D-LLM) is error-prone, especially for counting and existence questions. This motivates a single 3D vision-language-action model trained on curated, LLM-assisted data.
key_idea: LEO feeds egocentric 2D image tokens and object-centric 3D tokens (PointNet++ plus Spatial Transformer over segmented objects) into a LoRA-tuned Vicuna-7B. Every task, from captioning, QA, dialogue and planning to navigation and manipulation actions mapped onto rarely used text tokens, becomes prefix language modeling. Training runs in two stages: 3D VL alignment, then 3D VLA instruction tuning on ChatGPT-generated, scene-graph-grounded data.
insight: Object-centric 3D tokens are a simple, strong interface between 3D scenes and an LLM. Trained on the same data, LEO beats LL3DA and 3D-LLM, most clearly on ScanQA reasoning (CIDEr 99.2 vs 75.7 for LL3DA). For ObjNav, both modalities are essential: full model SR 23.1 / SPL 15.2 vs w/o 2D 7.8/4.6 and w/o 3D 8.6/6.8 on MP3D val. The global object-centric scene input acts like a coarse map, giving higher SPL (15.2 vs Habitat-web's 10.2). The feed-forward policy, which only sees the past 4 actions, cannot learn from exploratory human demos (SR drops to 7.1 with 70k human demos vs 23.1 with shortest paths). Ablations show three more things: (1) alignment helps (Scan2Cap Sim 65.4 vs 62.8 w/o Align); (2) ScanNet-only specialist tuning generalizes poorly to 3RScan (3RDialog 25.5 vs 73.3); (3) adding action data hurts VL (SQA3D EM 50.0 → 46.2 for VLA), the opposite of RT-2's finding. Test loss scales log-linearly with data, and gains saturate from 7B to 13B.
method: Unified token sequence: system message + optional egocentric 2D image tokens + object-centric 3D tokens + USER instruction → ASSISTANT response, trained with a prefix-LM autoregressive loss.
2D encoder: OpenCLIP ConvNeXt-base (LAION-2B) on the egocentric image, fine-tuned, with MLP adapters; CLIP text-feature 'semantic guidance' multiplies element-wise into image and object tokens.

3D encoder: frozen PointNet++ (ScanNet-pretrained, 1024 points/object) over Mask3D proposals or GT segments, then a trainable 3-layer, 8-head Spatial Transformer (Vil3DRef-style distance/angle-biased attention). A learnable embodiment 'self-object' token carries agent position and Fourier-embedded orientation (GPS+compass for navigation).
LLM: Vicuna-7B frozen with LoRA (rank 16, alpha 16) on all attention and MLP projections; ~7B total, ~142M trainable. Context is truncated to 256 tokens; inference uses beam search (5 beams).

Action tokenization (RT-2 style): 4 least-used SentencePiece tokens for ObjNav (forward, turn left, turn right, stop). 516 tokens for CLIPort (320 x-bins, 160 y-bins, 36 z-rotation bins). The policy is feed-forward and conditioned only on the current observation plus the past 4 actions.

Two-stage data: LEO-align (Cap3D/Objaverse 660K object captions, 354K object-referring expressions on ScanNet+3RScan, 20K 3RScan scene captions) and LEO-instruct (Scan2Cap, ScanQA/SQA3D/3RQA, 11K dialogues, 14K plans, ~60K MP3D ObjNav shortest-path episodes, 300K CLIPort demos).

LLM-assisted data pipeline: ChatGPT is prompted with 3DSSG scene graphs, subgraph sampling and object-centric CoT (object labels/IDs as thoughts). Regex- and scene-graph-based refinement then fixes counting and existence answers and removes negative or ID-leaking responses; negative-sample augmentation balances existence QA.

setting.backbone: Vicuna-7B (frozen + LoRA) with OpenCLIP ConvNeXt-base 2D encoder (fine-tuned), frozen PointNet++ and trainable Spatial Transformer
setting.model_size: ~7B total (~142M trainable); ablations with OPT-1.3B and Vicuna-13B
setting.training_data: LEO-align: 660K Objaverse/Cap3D object captions, 354K object-referring expressions (ScanNet+3RScan, incl. ChatGPT-generated), 20K ChatGPT scene captions. LEO-instruct: Scan2Cap 37K, 3D QA 83K (ScanQA, SQA3D, ~35K ChatGPT 3RScanQA), 11K dialogues, 14K plans, ~60K shortest-path ObjNav episodes from 57 MP3D train scenes, 300K CLIPort demos (100K per task).
setting.observation: egocentric RGB image + object-centric point clouds of all objects in the whole scene (global 3D view) + agent pose (GPS/compass via embodiment token) + past 4 actions
setting.action_space: ObjNav: discrete Habitat actions MOVE_FORWARD / TURN_LEFT / TURN_RIGHT / STOP as text tokens. CLIPort: discretized pick/place poses (x, y, z-rotation bins).
setting.simulator: Habitat (MP3D / HM3D ObjectNav); CLIPort (Ravens/PyBullet) for manipulation
setting.privileged: Object-centric point clouds of the entire scene are given at every step, which amounts to a pre-scanned global object map. For ObjNav the source of the object segments is not stated; 3D VL evaluation uses Mask3D proposals, while the data ablations use GT segments. GPS+compass pose is also provided.

numbers_note: Headline 3D VL numbers (Scan2Cap/ScanQA/SQA3D main table) exactly equal the 'w/o Act (Mask3D)' model, i.e. a model tuned without embodied acting data. Navigation and manipulation results come from the VLA-tuned model, so no single checkpoint produces all reported numbers. For ObjNav, 'MP3D-val' in the main table equals 'MP3D-seen' in the appendix table (the standard 21 categories). The scaling-law results appear only in a figure (test-loss curves, no numbers). CLIPort split is not stated explicitly; recorded as 'test'.
results: On MP3D ObjectNav val, LEO reaches SR 23.1 / SPL 15.2. That is below Habitat-web trained on 70k human demos in SR (35.4) but above it in SPL (10.2), and far above Habitat-web trained on shortest paths (4.4/2.2). Zero-shot on HM3D val it gets SR 23.1 / SPL 19.1 vs ZSON 25.5/12.6, and it can reach novel object categories (SR 11.1). On 3D VL it sets new SOTA without task-specific fine-tuning: Scan2Cap CIDEr 72.4 vs 3D-VisTA 66.9, ScanQA CIDEr 101.4 vs 69.6, SQA3D EM 50.0 vs 48.5. On CLIPort it is comparable to CLIPort, e.g. packing-google-objects-seq unseen 79.8 vs 71.9.
limitations: The ObjNav policy is feed-forward with only the past 4 actions and no recurrence or memory. SR is therefore lower than recurrent baselines, and the model fails to learn from exploratory human demonstrations (SR 7.1).

It assumes object-centric point clouds of the entire scene are available at every step, a pre-scanned global object map that standard ObjectNav agents do not get. This makes the navigation comparison not strictly apples-to-apples.

Co-training on embodied action data degrades 3D VL performance (e.g. SQA3D 50.0 → 46.2), so the headline VL and acting results come from different checkpoints. Generalization to novel scenes remains limited.
